shortDescription: Vietnam will cut its average retail electricity price by 2% from November 1 to support economic stability and reduce costs for households and businesses, the government said on Saturday.

children: Vietnam will cut its average retail electricity price by 2% from November 1 to support economic stability and reduce costs for households and businesses, the government said on Saturday.
The average retail tariff will fall to 2,159.9 dong ($0.085) per kilowatt-hour, excluding value-added tax, the government said in a statement
The government said the reduction followed a review of electricity pricing under existing regulations
The decision was intended to help maintain macroeconomic stability while supporting social welfare and business activity, it said
